αἳ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. pl.
αὐτός: αὐτός — self; intensive pron., masc. nom. sg.: ’he himself’
αὐτὰρ: αὐτάρ — but, and then; epic conj. (= Attic δέ, ἀλλά)
αὐτῷ: αὐτός — self; masc. dat. sg.: ’himself’, reinforcing a personal pronoun (σοὶ δ’ αὐτῷ ’to you yourself’)
αὖ: αὖ — again, in turn, back; adv., shorter form of αὖτε
αὖθ: αὖθι (elided αὖθ’) — here, on the spot, right here; adv. (distinct from αὖτε/αὖ ’again, in turn’)
βάζεις: βάζω — chatter, babble, talk; pres. 2 sg.
βάλε: βάλλω — throw, cast; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔβαλε): ’cast’
βροτοῖσιν: βροτός — mortal, mortal man; masc. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν) (= Attic -οῖς)
γ: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle (elided γ’)
γέρων: γέρων — old man; masc. nom. sg.
γε: γε — at least, in fact, indeed; limiting/emphatic particle
γεγαῶτ: γίγνομαι — become, be born; perf. part. masc. acc. sg., elided (γεγαῶτ’ = γεγαῶτα): ’having been born’
γενέσθαι: γίγνομαι — become, be born; aor. inf.: ’to have been born’
γερήνιος: Γερήνιος — Gerenian (standing epithet of Nestor); masc. nom. sg.; meaning uncertain — perhaps from Gerenia/Gerenon in Messenia, or linked to γέρων ’old man’ or γέρας ’honour’
γόνος: γόνος — offspring, child; masc. nom. sg.
γόοιο: γόος — wailing, lament; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
δάκρυ: δάκρυ — tear; neut. acc. sg., used collectively: ’tears’ · also elided δάκρυ’ = δάκρυα, neut. acc. pl.
δή: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δύστηνον: δύστηνος — wretched, unhappy; masc. acc. sg.
δώματ: δῶμα — house, home; neut. acc. pl., elided (δώματ’ = δώματα)
δὴ: δή — indeed, now, in fact; emphatic particle
δῆμον: δῆμος — people, land, community; masc. acc. sg.
δῶ: δῶ — house, home; indeclinable epic noun (= δῶμα), used as nom./acc. sg.
δῶκε: δίδωμι — give; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔδωκε)
εἰ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. · also introducing an indirect question after a verb of asking or telling: ’whether’ (εἰ δή ’whether indeed’) · also in εἰ δ’ ἄγε, an interjectional idiom with the imperative: ’come now, well then’
εἴ: εἰ — if; conditional conj. (accented εἴ before a following enclitic, περ among them) · also introducing an indirect question, ‘whether’ (τίς δ’ οἶδ’ εἴ κέ ... ‘who knows whether’)
εἴη: εἰμί — be; pres. opt. 3 sg.: ’it might be, he might be’; impersonal + inf.: ’it might be possible for him’
εἴποι: εἶπον — say, tell; aor. opt. 3 sg.
εἶπες: εἶπον (aor. of λέγω/φημί) — say, speak; aor. 2 sg.: ‘you said’ (augment fused into the diphthong, unlike unfused ἔειπες)
εὐρύοπα: εὐρύοπα — epithet of Zeus, literal sense disputed (’wide-voiced’ or ’far-seeing’); masc. nom. sg. in short -α
ζεύς: Ζεύς — Zeus, king of the gods; nom. sg.
ηὔδα: αὐδάω — speak, say; impf. 3 sg., augmented (αὐ- → ηὐ-)
θ: τε (elided and aspirated θ’ before rough breathing, cf. ἔφαθ’) — and; connective particle
θάμ: θαμά (elided θάμ’) — often, again and again; adv.
θαλάμοιο: θάλαμος — chamber, room; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θανάτοιο: θάνατος — death; masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
θείειν: θέω — run; pres. inf., epic θείειν (= Attic θεῖν): ’to run’ (πέρι θείειν ταχύς ’exceedingly swift to run’)
θεοῦ: θεός — god; masc. gen. sg., genitive with a verb of hearing · also genitive governed by a preposition (ἄνευ θεοῦ ’without a god’) · also possessive genitive with a noun: ’of the god’ (θεοῦ δαῖτα)
θεράπων: θεράπων — attendant, servant; masc. nom. sg.
θεὸς: θεός — god; masc. nom. sg., predicate: ’as a god’ · also plain nom. sg. subject, an unspecified deity left unnamed: ’a god’ (θεὸς δ’ ἐκέδασσεν Ἀχαιούς ’a god scattered the Achaeans’)
θυμόν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg.
θυμός: θυμός — heart, spirit; masc. nom. sg.
θυμὸν: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; acc. sg.
θυμῷ: θυμός — heart, spirit, soul; dat. sg.
κέ: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν); accented before an enclitic
κέλεται: κέλομαι — bid, command, urge; pres. 3 sg.
κακότητα: κακότης — badness, misery, trouble; fem. acc. sg.
κατὰ: κατά — down, throughout, in; prep. + acc.; also as preverb in tmesis (κατὰ … ἤσθιον = κατήσθιον ’devoured’) · also ’according to, in conformity with’ (κατὰ μοῖραν ’according to what is fitting’) · also + acc., ’in quest of, after’ (κατὰ ληίδα ’in quest of plunder’)
κε: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κείνου: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. gen. sg.
κεν: κε(ν) — epic particle marking a conditioned or potential action (= Attic ἄν)
κεῖνον: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. acc. sg.
κεῖνος: κεῖνος — that, that one; demonstrative pron., epic (= Attic ἐκεῖνος); masc. nom. sg.
κεῖται: κεῖμαι — lie; pres. 3 sg., used of the dead: ’lies (dead)’ · also in the idiom θεῶν ἐν γούνασι κεῖται: ’rests with the gods, lies in the gods’ hands’ (of an outcome, not of the dead) · also subj. (= κέηται): ’should lie’
κρονίων: Κρονίων — son of Cronus, Zeus; masc. nom. sg., by-form of Κρονίδης
κτήματα: κτῆμα — possession, property; neut. nom./acc. pl.
κυδαλίμοιο: κυδάλιμος — glorious, famous; adj., masc. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου)
λαῶν: λαός — people, host; masc. gen. pl., governed by ἄνασσε ’was lord over’ · also gen. with a noun: ’of the people’ (ποιμένα λαῶν ’shepherd of the people’)
μ: ἐγώ — I; encl. acc. sg., elided (μ’ = με): ’me’
μάλα: μάλα — very, very much, exceedingly; adv.
μέλαν: μέλας — black, dark; neut. nom./acc. sg.
μέλλεν: μέλλω — be about to, be destined to; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔμελλεν), + inf.: ’was on course to be’
μέν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ (the acute μέν is kept before a following enclitic; elsewhere μὲν) · also asseverative, = μήν ’truly, indeed’ (οὐ μέν ’not indeed’)
μεγάροις: μέγαρον — hall, great room; neut. dat. pl.: ‘in the halls’
μεγάροισι: μέγαρον — hall; dat. pl., epic -οισι (= Attic -οις)
μεγάροισιν: μέγαρον — hall, great room, house; neut. dat. pl., epic -οισι(ν), plural for a single house
μεγαλήτορος: μεγαλήτωρ — great-hearted, great of spirit (μέγας + ἦτορ ’heart’); masc. gen. sg.
μενέλαε: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta; masc. voc. sg.
μενέλαος: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. nom. sg.
μενελάου: Μενέλαος — Menelaus, king of Sparta, brother of Agamemnon; masc. gen. sg.
μερμήριξε: μερμηρίζω — ponder, devise, turn over in the mind; aor. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἐμερμήριξε)
μιν: μιν — him, her, it; epic encl. acc. pron. (= Attic αὐτόν/αὐτήν/αὐτό)
μνήσατο: μιμνήσκομαι — remember, call to mind (+ gen.); aor. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented
μοι: ἐγώ — I; encl. dat. sg.: ’to me, for me’
μὲν: μέν — on the one hand; particle, often answered by δέ
μὴ: μή — not; negative particle in wishes, prohibitions, and purpose/fear clauses
νέον: νέος — new, young; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’newly, for the first time’ · also masc. acc. sg., ’young’ (νέον ἄνδρα ’a young man’) · also neut. nom./acc. sg., ’new’ (οὔ τι νέον ’not a new one’, of a debt)
νέστωρ: Νέστωρ — Nestor, king of Pylos; masc. nom. sg.
νεστορίδης: Νεστορίδης — son of Nestor (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
νηυσὶ: ναῦς — ship; dat. pl., epic νηυσί (= Attic ναυσί)
νυ: νυ — now, then; weak encl. particle
νῶι: ἐγώ (dual νῶι) — we two; acc. dual: ’the two of us’ (μετὰ νῶι ’after the two of us’)  ·  also used as nom. dual: νῶι … ἱκόμεθ’ ’we two have come’
ξανθὸς: ξανθός — fair-haired, yellow, tawny; masc. nom. sg., standing epithet of Menelaus
οἰχομένοιο: οἴχομαι — be gone, have gone away; pres. part. gen. sg., epic -οιο (= Attic -ου), perfect sense: ’gone’
οἱ: οἱ — encl. dat. sg. pron. ’to/for him’ (very common) · also ὁ, ἡ, τό ’he, she, it’, masc. nom. pl. ’they’ (e.g. οἱ μὲν … οἱ δέ ’some … others’)
οἴχεται: οἴχομαι — be gone, have departed; pres. with perf. sense, 3 sg.: ’is gone’
οἵ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., masc. nom. pl.
οἵδε: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. pl.: ’these here’
οἶον: οἶος — alone, only; masc. acc. sg.
οἷσιν: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; possessive adj., neut./masc. dat. pl. (ν-movable): ’his own’ (agreeing with δώμασιν) · also relative, masc./neut. dat. pl.: whom (λαῶν οἷσιν ἄνασσε), not the possessive
οὐδ: οὐδέ (elided οὐδ’) — and not, nor, not even
οὐδέ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj.
οὐδὲ: οὐδέ — and not, nor, not even; neg. conj. (grave, mid-clause form)
οὔ: οὐ — not; neg. adv., in a question expecting the answer ’yes’ · also the plain negative adverb in a declarative statement, with no question implied: ’not’
οὔτ: οὔτε (elided οὔτ’) — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὔτε: οὔτε — nor, and not; correlative negative conj.
οὕτω: οὕτω(ς) — thus, so, in this way; adv.
πάντα: πᾶς — all, every; neut. nom./acc. pl.
πάϊς: παῖς — child, son; nom. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic παῖς)
πέρι: περί — around, about, exceedingly; adv. with anastrophe (accent thrown back): ’beyond all others’ (πέρι κέρδεα οἶδεν)
παρέθηκε: παρατίθημι — set beside, serve; aor. 3 sg.
πεισίστρατος: Πεισίστρατος — Peisistratus, son of Nestor; masc. nom. sg.
πεπνυμένα: πέπνυμαι — be prudent, wise (perf. w/ pres. sense, from πνέω ’breathe’); part. neut. acc. pl.: ’prudent (counsels)’
πεπνυμένον: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. acc. sg., here transferred to a speech: ’showing sound sense’
πεπνυμένος: πέπνυμαι — have one’s wits about one, be prudent; perf. part. masc. nom. sg. (trad. linked to πνέω ’breathe’, though uncertain), stock epithet: ’prudent’
περ: περ — even, though; concessive particle, esp. with a participle (= Attic καίπερ) · also used to intensify an adverb or pronoun rather than concede a point: ἔνθα περ ’in the very place where, just where’
περὶ: περί — around, about; prep. + gen.: ’superior to, beyond’; also as adv.: ’exceedingly, surpassingly’ · also prep. + gen. in its plain sense ’about, concerning’ (περὶ πατρός ’about his father’) · also preverb in tmesis · + dat. · also + acc., of place, ’around, about’ (περὶ ἄστυ ’around the city’)
πολέας: πολύς — much, many; masc./fem. acc. pl., epic πολέας (= Attic πολλούς)
πολλὰ: πολύς — much, many; neut. acc. pl.: ’many things, greatly’
πρίν: πρίν — before, until; conj./adv., + inf. (like Attic πρίν) · also + a temporal clause (πρίν γ’ ὅτ’ ἄν + subj.): ’until the time when’ · also πρίν κε + opt., an independent potential clause answering a suppressed protasis: ’sooner, before then’ (πρίν κεν ... ἵκοιο ’you would arrive home before then’)
προκείμενα: πρόκειμαι — lie before, be set out; pres. part. neut. nom./acc. pl.
προσέφη: πρόσφημι — speak to, address; aor. 3 sg.
πρὶν: πρίν — before, until; adv./conj., + inf. (grave, mid-clause form) · also τὸ πρίν, substantivized with the article: ‘formerly, at first’, no infinitive · also bare adv. ’formerly’, no art./inf.
πρῶτ: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. pl. used adverbially, elided (πρῶτ’ = πρῶτα): ’first’
πρῶτον: πρῶτος — first; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’first’
πόποι: πόποι — (in ὢ πόποι) exclamation of surprise or displeasure: ’ah! well!’; origin unknown
πόσιν: πόσις — husband; acc. sg. · also the distinct noun πόσις ’a drinking, drink’ (from πίνω); acc. sg.: ’drink’ (paired with βρῶσις ’eating’)
πότμον: πότμος — fate, doom, death; masc. acc. sg.
πώ: πώ — yet, up to now; enclitic adv. (usually with a negative)
πᾶσιν: πᾶς — all, every; masc./neut. dat. pl. (ν-movable)
σέβας: σέβας — awe, reverent wonder; neut. nom. sg. (σέβας μ’ ἔχει ’awe holds me’)
σέθεν: σύ — you (sg.); gen. sg., epic σέθεν (= Attic σοῦ)
σὺ: σύ — you (sg.); nom. sg. (grave, mid-clause form)
σὺν: σύν — with, together with; prep. + dat.
τ: τε (elided τ’) — and; ’epic τε’ also marks a standing fact · after οὔ νυ perhaps τοι ’to you’ · also in a question, an expressive epic τε with no connective force, giving a note of doubt or wonder (πῶς τε ...; ’how, pray...?’)
τί: τίς, τί — who? what?; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially ’why’ · also the enclitic indefinite τις, τι ’someone, something’ (accented τί before an enclitic): neut. acc. sg. used adverbially with a negative, ’at all’ (οὔ τι) · adj.
τε: τε — and, both...and; enclitic connective; also ’epic τε’ marking a standing general truth in relative clauses
τηλέμαχός: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. nom. sg. (accented before enclitic θ’)
τηλεμάχῳ: Τηλέμαχος — Telemachus, son of Odysseus; masc. dat. sg.
τι: τις, τι — someone, something; neut. acc. sg., used adverbially with negatives ’at all’ · also adjectival indefinite: ’some, any’ (τι δήμιον ἄλλο ’some other public matter’) · also adverbial without a negative: ’in some way, in some measure’ (τι κατὰ πρῆξιν ’on some business’)
τινά: τις, τι — someone, something; masc. acc. sg., indefinite, accented before enclitic οἱ (with ὅν: ὅν τινα ’whatever’)
τινες: τις, τι — someone, something; masc. nom. pl. (after a relative, οἵ τινες = ὅστις pl.): ’whoever’
τοι: σύ — you (sg.); encl. dat. sg.: ’to/for you’ · also τοι, the affirming particle: ’you know, indeed’ (esp. in ἦ τοι, οὔ τοι); the two are not always easy to keep apart
τοῖσι: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. dat. pl. ’to/among them’
τοῦ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. gen. sg. ’of him, that one’
τοῦτό: οὗτος, αὕτη, τοῦτο — this; neut. nom./acc. sg., accented before enclitic γ’
τόν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg.: ’him’; also relative: ’whom’
τὰ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. pl.: ’these things’ · also in the adverbial idiom τὰ πρῶτα, ’at first, first’ (not ’these things’) · also with a noun, pointing to it: ’those, the’ (τὰ σὰ γούνατα ’those knees of yours’)
τὴν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. acc. sg. ’her’
τὸ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg. (τὸ πάροιθεν ’that which was before’)
τὸν: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. acc. sg. ’him’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅ: whom, which; masc. acc. sg. (τὸν Ἀλφειὸς τέκε ’whom Alpheus begot’)
τῇ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); fem. dat. sg.: ’her, with her’
τῷ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc./neut. dat. sg.; also relative: ’in which’ · the relative dat. sg. also serves as an instrumental, ’with which’ (τῷ δάμνησι ’with which she overpowers’)
φάτο: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., unaugmented (= ἔφατο)
φέρε: φέρω — bring, carry; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= ἔφερε)
φέρουσα: φέρω — carry, bear; pres. part. fem. nom. sg.: ’carrying, bringing’
φίλ: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. voc. sg., elided (φίλ’ = φίλε)
φίλου: φίλος — dear, one’s own; masc. gen. sg.
φρένα: φρήν — mind, wits, heart; acc. sg.
χερσί: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl. (without movable ν)
χερσὶ: χείρ — hand; fem. dat. pl., epic -σί (= Attic χερσίν)
ἀέθλους: ἄθλος — trial, contest, ordeal; masc. acc. pl., uncontracted epic ἄεθλος (= Attic ἄθλους)
ἀγλαὸς: ἀγλαός — splendid, radiant; masc. nom. sg.
ἀγορεύεις: ἀγορεύω — speak out, declare, say; pres. 2 sg.
ἀγόρευεν: ἀγορεύω — speak (esp. in assembly); impf. 3 sg., unaugmented
ἀλλήλοισιν: ἀλλήλων — one another; reciprocal pron., masc. dat. pl., epic -οισιν
ἀμφ: ἀμφί (elided ἀμφ’) — around, about, concerning; + dat. · also + acc., ’around, with, accompanying’ (ἀμφ’ Ὀδυσῆα ’with, around Odysseus’)
ἀμφίπολος: ἀμφίπολος — handmaid, woman in attendance; nom. sg.
ἀμύμονος: ἀμύμων — blameless, excellent (an old epithet whose exact force is uncertain); gen. sg.
ἀνέρος: ἀνήρ — man; masc. gen. sg., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἀνδρός)
ἀντίον: ἀντίον — face to face, in answer, opposite; adv.
ἀπαμειβόμενος: ἀπαμείβομαι — answer, reply; pres. part. nom. sg. masc.
ἀπὸ: ἀπό — from, away from; + gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, separated from its verb (ἀπὸ … ὀλέσσει = ἀπολέσει ’will destroy’; ἀπὸ … δοθείη = ἀποδοθείη ’be given back’)
ἀργείων: Ἀργεῖοι — the Argives, i.e. the Greeks; gen. pl.
ἀσαμίνθους: ἀσάμινθος — bathtub (origin unknown); fem. acc. pl.
ἀτρεΐδης: Ἀτρεΐδης — son of Atreus (patronymic); masc. nom. sg.
ἀχαιοὶ: Ἀχαιοί — the Achaeans, the Greeks; masc. nom. pl.
ἂν: ἄν — modal particle marking contingency (with subj. = future contingency, with opt. = potential) · also with a secondary indicative (impf./aor.) marking an unreal, contrary-to-fact conclusion: ’would’ (οὐκ ἂν ... ἀγόρευες ’you would not be speaking’) · also = ἀνά (preposition/preverb ’up’) in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἂν … βαῖνε = ἀνέβαινε, ἂν … βάντες = ἀναβάντες)
ἄλγε: ἄλγος — pain, grief; neut. nom./acc. pl. (ἄλγεα, elided ἄλγε’)
ἄλλο: ἄλλος — other, another; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἄλλοι: ἄλλος — other, another; masc. nom. pl.
ἄρ: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, elided form ἄρ’ before a vowel
ἄρα: ἄρα — so, as it turned out, then; inferential particle
ἄργεϊ: Ἄργος — Argos; neut. dat. sg., epic uncontracted -εϊ (= Attic -ει)
ἅλα: ἅλς — sea, salt sea; fem. acc. sg.
ἅμ: ἅμα (elided ἅμ’) — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἅμα: ἅμα — together with, at the same time as; adv./prep. + dat.
ἐγώ: ἐγώ — I; nom. sg. (accented ἐγώ before the enclitic τοι that follows)
ἐικυῖα: ἔοικα — be like, resemble; perf. part. fem. nom. sg., + dat.: ’likened to, having the appearance of’
ἐκ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as adverb or preverb in tmesis, no case expressed: ’out’ (ἐκ δ’ ἔβαν ’and out they stepped’)
ἐλθὼν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; aor. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’having come’
ἐμεῖο: ἐγώ — I; epic gen. sg. ἐμεῖο (= Attic ἐμοῦ)
ἐμισγόμεθ: μίσγω — mix, mingle; mid. meet, associate with (+ dat.); impf. 1 pl. mid., elided (ἐμισγόμεθ’ = ἐμισγόμεθα)
ἐμοί: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg., accented (non-enclitic emphatic): ’to me’
ἐμοὶ: ἐγώ — I; dat. sg.: ’to, for me’
ἐμόγησεν: μογέω — toil, labor, suffer hardship; aor. 3 sg., augmented (ν-movable): ’toiled’
ἐμὸν: ἐμός — my, mine; masc./neut. acc. sg.
ἐμὸς: ἐμός — my, mine; masc. nom. sg.
ἐν: ἐν — in, on, among; + dat.; also used as an adverb, ’in it, there’ · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐν … βάλῃ = ἐμβάλῃ ’cast in’; ἐν … χεῦον = ἔγχεον ’pour in’)
ἐνθάδ: ἐνθάδε (elided ἐνθάδ’) — here, to this place; adv.
ἐνὶ: ἐν (epic ἐνί) — in, on, among; + dat.
ἐξ: ἐκ (ἐξ before a vowel) — out of, from; + gen. · also as a preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐξ … ἕντο = ἐξέντο, from ἐξίημι ’send out, put away (desire)’)
ἐοικότα: ἔοικα — be like, be fitting; perf. part. masc. acc. sg.: ’fitting’ (ἐοικότα μυθήσασθαι ’to speak fittingly’)
ἐπ: ἐπί (elided ἐπ’) — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as preverb in tmesis, standing apart from its verb (ἐπ’ … χεῦε = ἐπέχευε ‘poured upon’)
ἐπέεσσι: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. dat. pl., epic -εσσι (= Attic ἔπεσι)
ἐπιμνησθεὶς: ἐπιμιμνήσκομαι — think of, call to mind; aor. pass. part. nom. sg. masc.; + gen.
ἐπὶ: ἐπί — on, upon, over, towards, against; + dat./acc./gen. · also as adverb, no case expressed: ’to it, over it; besides’ (θεοὶ δ’ ἐπὶ μάρτυροι ’witnesses to it’; ἐπὶ κτέρεα κτερεΐξαι ’besides’)
ἐρέω: ἐρέω — say, tell, declare; fut. 1 sg. (epic fut. of εἶπον, = Attic ἐρῶ); in tmesis with ἐκ, ἐξερέω ’speak out plainly’
ἐτήτυμον: ἐτήτυμος — true, real; neut. acc. sg. used adverbially: ’truly’
ἐτύχθη: τεύχω — make, bring about; aor. pass. 3 sg.: ‘came to pass’
ἐφ: ἐπί (elided ἐφ’ before a rough breathing) — on, upon, over; + acc.
ἐόντες: εἰμί — be; pres. part. masc. nom. pl., epic (= Attic ὄντες): ’being’
ἑλένῃ: Ἑλένη — Helen, wife of Menelaus; fem. dat. sg.
ἑτοῖμα: ἕτοιμος — ready, at hand; neut. acc. pl.
ἔθηκεν: τίθημι — put, place; aor. 3 sg., augmented: ’placed’
ἔλειπε: λείπω — leave, leave behind; impf. 3 sg., augmented: ’he left’
ἔοικε: ἔοικα — be fitting, seem; perf. with pres. sense, impersonal 3 sg.: ’it is fitting’
ἔπεα: ἔπος — word, speech; neut. acc. pl., epic uncontracted (= Attic ἔπη)
ἔπος: ἔπος — word, speech, thing said; neut. nom./acc. sg.
ἔργον: ἔργον — deed, work, task; neut. acc. sg. · also neut. nom. sg., subject of an impersonal verb (κακὸν … ἔργον τε ἔπος τε μελέτω ’let no evil deed or word be a care’)
ἔσσεται: εἰμί — be; fut. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἔσται)
ἔστι: εἰμί — be; pres. 3 sg. impersonal: ’it is possible’ · also existential, ‘there is’ (ἔστι δέ τις πέτρη ‘there is a rock’)
ἔφατ: φημί — say, speak; impf. 3 sg. mid., augmented, elided (ἔφατ’ = ἔφατο)
ἔχεν: ἔχω — have, hold; impf. 3 sg., unaugmented (= εἶχεν): ’held’
ἔχευεν: χέω — pour; aor. 3 sg., in tmesis with ἐν (ἐν … ἔχευεν = ἐνέχευεν): ’poured in’
ἕκαστα: ἕκαστος — each, every; neut. acc. pl. used substantivally: ’each thing, everything’
ἕπεσθαι: ἕπομαι — follow, accompany, go with; pres. inf.: ’to go with, accompany’
ἠέ: ἠέ — or; disjunctive conj. (epic = ἤ), esp. in ἠέ ... ἦ ’either... or’
ἠριγένεια: ἠριγένεια — early-born; fem. nom. sg., epithet of Dawn
ἡμέας: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; acc. pl., epic ἡμέας (= Attic ἡμᾶς)
ἡμέτερον: ἡμέτερος — our, ours; neut. acc. sg.
ἡμεῖς: ἐγώ (pl. ἡμεῖς) — I, we; nom. pl. ’we’
ἤ: ἤ — or; disjunctive conj., accented before an enclitic (ἤ κεν); ἤ … ἦε ’whether … or’
ἤλυθεν: ἔρχομαι — go, come; epic aor. 3 sg. (= Attic ἦλθεν): ’came’
ἤματα: ἦμαρ — day; neut. acc. pl., acc. of time: ’all the days, every day’
ἥ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ — who, which; relative pron., fem. nom. sg. · also ὁ, ἡ, τό (personal/demonstrative pronoun): she; fem. nom. sg. (ἥ γε ’she indeed’, of the ship)
ἦ: ἦ — truly, verily; affirming particle · also interrogative particle introducing an earnest question · also = ἤ ’or’, in the correlative ἠέ … ἦ ’whether … or’ · also ἠμί — say, speak; unaugmented aor./impf. 3 sg. (= ἔφη), closing or introducing direct speech: ’he/she said’ (ἦ ῥα ’so he said’)
ἦεν: εἰμί — be; impf. 3 sg., epic (= Attic ἦν)
ἧος: ἧος — as long as, while; temporal conj., epic (= Attic ἕως)
ἰδέσθαι: ὁράω — see; aor. mid. inf.: ‘to see’
ἱκανέμεν: ἱκάνω — come, arrive, reach; pres. inf., epic -έμεν (= Attic ἱκάνειν): ’to go and arrive’
ἱππότα: ἱππότης — horseman, charioteer (epithet of Nestor); masc. nom. sg., old form in short -α
ἴαλλον: ἰάλλω — send forth, put out (the hand); impf. 3 pl., unaugmented
ἴδμεν: οἶδα — know; pres. 1 pl., epic ἴδμεν (= Attic ἴσμεν): ’we know’
ἴδον: ὁράω — see; aor. 1 sg., unaugmented, from the root of εἶδον (= εἶδον) · also aor. 3 pl. (the same ending serves both persons): ’they saw’
ὀδυρόμενος: ὀδύρομαι — lament, mourn; pres. part. masc. nom. sg.: ’lamenting’
ὀδυσσῆος: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; gen. sg. (double-σ, metrical variant of single-σ Ὀδυσῆος)
ὀδυσῆι: Ὀδυσσεύς — Odysseus; dat. sg. (single-σ metrical variant of Ὀδυσσῆι)
ὀνείαθ: ὄνειαρ — good thing, benefit; of food, neut. acc. pl., elided (ὀνείαθ’ = ὀνείατα)
ὀτρηρὸς: ὀτρηρός — brisk, active, ready; masc. nom. sg.
ὁ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); masc. nom. sg.
ὁρμαίνοντες: ὁρμαίνω — ponder, turn over in the mind, debate; pres. part. masc. nom. pl.: ’pondering’
ὃ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅ (relative) — who, which; neut. nom./acc. sg., referring to a person: ’that he...’ · also masc. nom. sg. relative, ’who’, used in address with a 2nd person verb (ὃ χθιζὸς θεὸς ἤλυθες ’you who came yesterday as a god’)
ὃς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.) · also plain demonstrative, ’he’ (ὃς γὰρ δεύτατος ἦλθεν), not a relative
ὄλβον: ὄλβος — prosperity, good fortune, happiness; masc. acc. sg.
ὄφρα: ὄφρα — so that, in order that; epic (= Attic ἵνα); + subj. · also temporal, ’until’, + indic. (ὄφρα ... βάλε): marking the point an action ceases · also temporal + subj. with κε, correlative with τόφρα: ’as long as, until’ (ὄφρα κε κείνη τοῦτον ἔχῃ νόον ’for as long as she holds this purpose’)
ὅ: ὁ, ἡ, τό — he, she, it; that (in Homer a pronoun; later the article); neut. nom./acc. sg.; with γε: ’he’ · also relative, masc. nom. sg., accented before an enclitic: ’who’ (ὅ κε ... ἐφείη) · also = ὅτι ’that’; εἰς ὅ ’until’ · also relative, neut. nom./acc. sg.: ’which’ (ὅ οἱ πέρι δῶκεν Ἀθήνη ’which Athena gave her beyond others’)
ὅδ: ὅδε — this, this here; demonstrative pron., masc. nom. sg., elided (ὅδ’ = ὅδε)
ὅθι: ὅθι — where; epic relative adverb (= Attic οὗ)
ὅς: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (relative) — who, which; masc. nom. sg. · also possessive ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: his own, her own (masc. nom. sg.)
ὅσα: ὅσος — as much/many as; neut. acc. pl.: ’all that, as much as’
ὅτ: ὅτε (elided ὅτ’) — when; temporal conj., here + ἄν and subj. in a general/future clause · also + indic., of a single definite past event: ’when’ (ὅτ’ ἐν Ἄργεϊ ... ἵστασαν ’when they were mooring in Argos’)
ὅτε: ὅτε — when; temporal conjunction · also ’since, now that’ (ὅτε πρότερός γε πύθοιτο ’since he learned of it first’)
ὑπ: ὑπό (elided ὑπ’) — under, beneath; prep. + gen.; also + acc., ’under, up under’ · also of agent with a verb of dying, ‘by, at the hands of’ + gen. (ὤλεθ’ ὑπ’ Αἰγίσθοιο ‘perished by Aegisthus’) · also + dat., ’under, beneath’
ὑπεὶρ: ὑπέρ — over, above; prep. + acc., epic lengthened by-form ὑπείρ
ὑπὸ: ὑπό — under, beneath; prep. + dat./acc.; also used as an adverb, ’beneath’ · also as preverb in tmesis (ὑπὸ … ἐδήσατο = ὑπεδήσατο ’bound beneath’)
ὑφ: ὑπό (elided ὑφ’, before a rough breathing) — under, beneath; + gen., dat. or acc.
ὕδωρ: ὕδωρ — water; neut. acc. sg. · also nom. sg. (identical neut. form), subject of a verb (ἄνεμός τε καὶ ὕδωρ ‘wind and current’)
ὡς: ὡς — as, how, that, when; with the optative introduces a wish: ’so may…’ (unaccented; accented ὥς / ὣς is ’thus’) · also ὡς + unaugmented ὄφελον + inf., an unfulfillable wish: ’would that...’ · also ὡς + opt., a purpose clause (= ἵνα): ’so that’ (ὡς τὸν χόλον ἐξακέσαιτο ’so that he might appease the anger’) · also exclamatory ὡς + adj. + inf.: ’how (good, etc.) it is to...’ (ὡς ἀγαθὸν ... λιπέσθαι ’how good a thing it is to be left behind’)
ὢ: ὤ — oh! ah! (exclamation, as in ὢ πόποι)
ὣς: ὥς — thus, so; adverb (accented, distinct from unaccented ὡς ’as’; = Attic οὕτως) · also postpositive after its noun (anastrophe), = comparative ὡς ’as, like’: ὄρνις δ’ ὥς ’like a bird’
ὦρσε: ὄρνυμι — stir up, rouse, set in motion; aor. 3 sg.: ’stirred up, roused’
ὧδ: ὧδε — so, thus, in this way; adv., elided (ὧδ’ = ὧδε)
ὧδε: ὧδε — here, to this place, in this way; adv.
ᾧ: ὅς, ἥ, ὅν (possessive) — his own, her own; masc. dat. sg.: ’his own (son)’ · also relative ὅς, ἥ, ὅν: whom, which; masc. dat. sg. (δοίη δ’ ᾧ κ’ ἐθέλοι ’give her to whom he wished’)
ῥ: ἄρα (weakened ῥα, elided ῥ’) — then, indeed, so; inferential particle
ῥά: ἄρα — then, so, as it seems; inferential particle, weak enclitic form ῥα, accented ῥά
